Findings accepted (batch `ae8e0928…`). Summary of the four submitted analyst findings:

1. **Timing (supported)** — Point-in-time and execution constraints: inputs only from observed closes at/before the signal close (current download, not vintage); execution no earlier than the next observed close; terminal-row signals have no execution observation; the observed date union is not an exchange calendar, so absences prove nothing and no filling is allowed; warmup exclusions are separate from closes required per signal.
2. **Units (supported)** — Unadjusted CNY/share closes at one symbol/observed-date grain; the baseline score is a dimensionless ratio of closes with no annualization; close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions; bundle lacks volume, bid/ask, costs; data are exploratory development observations, never a holdout.
3. **Normalization (hypothesis)** — At most one alternative: cross-symbol one-observation return dispersion/volatility heterogeneity is the stronger motivation, pointing at `normalization` + a new `volatility_window` parameter (positive-volatility eligibility, deeper warmup, scale-only transform — not a Sharpe ratio, no systematic-risk removal); isolated large single-observation moves are the weaker competing motivation, pointing at `max_absolute_daily_return` as an eligibility exclusion. Neither motivation touches `lookback` or `direction`; no superiority claim.
4. **Interpretation (supported)** — Any adoption/superiority/investment-benefit claim would require a separate future evaluation with forward labels, point-in-time universe, transaction costs/bid/ask, adjusted or corporate-action-annotated prices, an official calendar, and untouched out-of-sample data; descriptive statistics here cannot establish superiority, alpha or tradability.

All statements are qualitative with exact source quotes; exploratory, unproven status preserved throughout.
